name: Rice
notes: Rice tolerates standing water and responds strongly to assured water supply; alternating wetting and drying reduces methane emissions and water use.

name: Wheat
notes: Terminal heat above 30 C during grain filling sharply reduces grain weight; an irrigation timed around crown root initiation is usually the highest priority.

name: Maize
notes: Maize is most sensitive to water shortage at tasselling and silking; a single missed irrigation in this window can dominate season yield.

name: Sorghum
notes: Sorghum is a drought-resilient crop suited to semi-arid tracts with erratic rainfall.

name: Cotton
notes: Square and boll development stages are highly sensitive to both moisture deficit and boll rot after wet spells.

name: Groundnut
notes: Excess water around the root zone causes red rot; a well-drained sandy loam is preferred.

name: Chickpea
notes: Chickpea is largely grown on residual moisture; excess water causes damping off and wilt.

name: Tomato
notes: Irregular moisture plus high humidity favours fruit rot; avoid overhead irrigation late in the day.

name: Soybean
notes: Soybean fixes its own nitrogen but still needs a reliable supply of water at pod filling.

name: Pearl Millet
notes: Highly heat and drought tolerant; grows on light soils with low fertility.

name: Finger Millet
notes: Finger millet is a staple in rainfed tracts and stores well as grain.

name: Pigeonpea
notes: Pigeonpea is deep rooted and drought tolerant once established.

name: Mustard
notes: Terminal heat and moisture stress at pod filling cause severe yield loss.

name: Potato
notes: Potato prefers a slightly acidic, well-aerated soil; tuber quality falls sharply when soil pH exceeds 7.0 (tuber blotch).
